summary: The recorded base reproduces the application-level corruption when the reported XCCL MIN-to-SUM behavior is simulated. The candidate is a plausible XPU-only gather-plus-local-min workaround and its mocked regression passes, but the issue-defining two-rank Intel XPU/XCCL path could not be run. A two-rank Gloo adversarial run rejects the candidate's stacked all_gather_into_tensor output layout, making backend-specific XCCL validation necessary.

tests.what_was_measured: On the exact base, simulated XCCL integer MIN fallback to SUM changed token IDs [42, 7] to [84, 14], reproducing the sampler-level failure contract.
At the exact candidate commit, all four candidate mock-based regression cases passed.

A real two-rank Gloo collective rejected candidate output shape (world_size, batch) with invalid tensor size; this is a portability counterexample and shows the mocks do not validate collective layout.
On one assigned gfx950 GPU with RCCL world size one, a three-element int64 token tensor remained [42, 7, 0] through the candidate path. This does not validate multi-rank or XCCL.

gpu_execution.evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950, Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2, one visible GPU; the candidate path ran with RCCL world size one. No Intel XPU execution occurred.

remaining_counterexamples: The issue-defining Intel XPU/XCCL two-rank path was not executable in the prepared ROCm environment.
Two-rank Gloo rejects the candidate's stacked all_gather_into_tensor output shape; XCCL acceptance of that exact shape remains unverified.
The candidate regression mocks all distributed operations and covers only scalar per-rank token tensors, not a real batched collective or serving path.
remaining_limitations: No Intel XPU hardware, PyTorch XPU build, XCCL/oneCCL runtime, or second assigned GPU was available.
The single-gfx950 run cannot qualify another architecture or a distributed workload.
No native code changed, so native rebuild requirements were not applicable.
